Use only your own ADR number so the four files do not collide. ADR 0003 (mobile layout) already exists on `main`; read it too. Read the other tracks' rows so you know who owns what; if your design needs something from another track, write it under "Dependencies" in your ADR instead of building it yourself.

## Phase 1: ADR proposal (now)

1. Read `docs/current-status.md`, `docs/current-architecture.md`, `docs/development.md`, `docs/adr/0001-*.md`, `docs/adr/0002-*.md` and the code your area touches.
2. Write `docs/adr/000N-<short-slug>.md` (the number from the table). Match the tone of ADR 0002: plain, factual, no marketing. Status: `Proposed`. Sections:
   - **Context**: what exists today, with file:line references.
   - **Options considered**: at least two real options, with trade-offs.
   - **Decision** (proposed): the option you recommend, and why.
   - **Scope / out of scope.**
   - **Owner actions**: anything only the owner can do (Google Cloud console, GitHub secrets, a keystore password, a physical phone). Say exactly what and when it is needed. Never invent credentials, client IDs or keys.
   - **Dependencies** on other tracks, and what they need from you.
   - **Implementation plan**: ordered stages, each small enough for one sub-agent run, each with its own check (test, command or screenshot).
   - **Validation plan**: unit/integration tests, browser screenshots, Android emulator screenshots and screen recordings (videos) where the change is visible or a flow.
   - **Risks and open questions** for the owner.
3. Commit, push the branch (retry on transient remote errors), and end your turn with one line: `ADR READY: docs/adr/000N-....md @ <commit sha>`, followed by a short summary and your open questions.
4. Do **not** start implementing. No cargo or Android builds in this phase. Wait for a message from the coordinator: either review comments (revise, push, report `ADR READY` again) or `GREENLIGHT`.

## Phase 2: implementation (only after GREENLIGHT)

- Split the implementation plan into stages and hand each stage to a sub-agent with `delegate_task`: provider instance `codex`, model `gpt-6.1-terra`, option `reasoningEffort: high`, working in **your** worktree (no new checkout). Run stages one after another, not in parallel, in the same worktree. Give each sub-agent: these rules, the ADR, the exact stage, its check, and "commit when the check passes; do not push; no further delegation".
- After each stage, **review it yourself**: read the diff, run the stage's check, and fix or send it back. You own the result.
- When all stages pass: run the full gates (`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 mise run check:all`, plus the rendered tests below), do the validation plan (screenshots and videos), set the ADR status to `Accepted` with the decisions taken, update `docs/current-status.md` and `docs/development.md` where they change, push, and open a PR to `main`: `gh pr create -R BbrSofiane/email-os --base main`. The PR body lists what changed, the gates run with results, and the validation evidence (paths to screenshots/videos).
- End your turn with: `READY FOR REVIEW: <PR url> @ <head sha>` and the open items. The coordinator reviews and merges; you do not merge.

## Machine limits (shared by all tracks)

- 4 cores, 15 GB RAM, ~8 GB free disk. Only two tracks implement at the same time; the coordinator decides which.
- Rust: always `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`. One heavy command (cargo build/test, Android build, full test suite) at a time: before one, check `pgrep -fa 'cargo|gradle|vitest'`; if another track is building, wait and retry.
- Android build from a worktree: first `cp -n /home/exedev/email-os/src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/java/dev/exedev/emailos/androidfixture/generated/* src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/java/dev/exedev/emailos/androidfixture/generated/` (the shared target does not regenerate these), then `mise run android:build`.
- Do not create large files outside your worktree. Delete build outputs you no longer need.

## Android emulator (shared, one track at a time)

- Device host `local`, id `emulator-5554` (Android 15, x86_64, 1080×2400). Drive it with the T3 device tools (`device_open`, then the returned `agent-device` command; `device_screenshot`). `adb` only for install, logs and `run-as` file checks.
- Lock: before using it, create `/home/exedev/email-os-usable/emulator.lock` containing your branch name (`set -o noclobber; echo usable/xyz > …/emulator.lock`). If it exists and is not yours, wait. Remove it when done. Leave the app installed and the emulator as you found it (input method, airplane mode off).
- Releasing: before removing the lock, run the agent-device `close` command and then `device_close` (never `shutdown`). Closing only the Device panel leaves the device claimed and blocks the other tracks with DEVICE_IN_USE. If you get DEVICE_IN_USE, never take over or close another session, kill processes or edit claim files: stop with `BLOCKED:` and the exact error.
- Before coordinate taps or `back`, confirm the app is in the foreground. Element refs (`@eN`) go stale after a screenshot: re-snapshot first.
- Screen recordings: `agent-device record` (see `help record`). Keep videos short (≤60 s).

## Validation evidence

- Browser screenshots: `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/tmp/chrome-rendered/chrome/linux-156.0.8078.80/chrome-linux64/chrome EMAIL_OS_SCREENSHOT_DIR=<dir> mise run screenshots:mobile`. Rendered tests: `EMAIL_OS_RUN_RENDERED=1 EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=<same chrome> pnpm vitest run --config vitest.config.ts <file>`.
- Put committed evidence under `docs/validation/<track-slug>/` (small PNGs; videos only if under ~5 MB, otherwise keep them in `/home/exedev/email-os-usable/<track-slug>/` and list the path in the PR).
- Synthetic data only in anything committed. Never commit real mail, tokens, client secrets, keystores or passwords. Never open any directory named `email-os-mobile-refs`.

## Working style

- Readable multi-line code that matches the surrounding style; no minified one-liners. Tests next to the existing ones.
- Product voice: terse and factual; never claim more than the app knows (pending, confirmed, failed and unknown stay distinct). No third-party brand names in UI copy.
- Do not use the repo's `implement` skill. Delegate only as described in phase 2.
- You run with full access. Never request escalated or sandbox-bypass permissions (nobody can approve them and you will stall). Keep temporary files inside your worktree (e.g. under `.git/`), not in `/tmp`. Pass PR bodies inline or from a file inside the worktree.
- If you are blocked on something only the owner can provide, say `BLOCKED:` with the exact need and stop; do not work around it with fake values.

The leftovers are gone: a subagent deleted all seven folders, and the disk now has 4.6 GB free (94% full). It first checked that each one was real, held nothing that couldn't be recreated, and wasn't in use by any process it could see. It left everything else alone.

The deleted Android output included the 18 November debug app file (about 608 MB). Anything that installs from that path needs a new build first.

The [HTML thread](t3-thread://v2/a54b6c0e-579e-4ecd-b328-bf6fee0ad1e4/mcp:launch:33fa7c628557f8fe0aee05e4f255dc8f2c864ad747677874dcf869889f71ea9c) now has the emulator and is re-recording:
- **Empty message:** the newsletter now shows up on Android when reopened, by the thread's account. I haven't seen the recording yet.
- **New problem:** in one take, "Open in browser" didn't leave the app, although it had worked in the dry run. The thread is checking whether the tap missed or there's a real bug with reopened messages. If it's a real bug, it blocks the merge until it's fixed.

I'm not notified when the thread finishes, so message me when you want me to check it and, if it passes, merge.

## Changes

- Rename the Android package to `dev.exedev.emailos` in mechanical commit `7f0680c`. Set the launcher label to Email OS and use the existing art for the adaptive icon.
- Build universal ARM64 and x86_64 APKs with JKS or PKCS12 signing and 16 KB native-library alignment. Add protected, main-only GitHub Release delivery with automatic version codes and a throwaway-key PR CI job.
- Disable Android backup and add cloud and device-transfer exclusions. Move Android app-data path lookup and database opening off the Tauri event loop. Preserve legacy fixture disclosure and retry behavior.

## Verification

- Verified APK metadata, signer, ABIs, alignment, backup rules and debug versus release cleartext settings. Both keystore formats passed locally with throwaway keys.
- A same-signer 1004 → 1005 update on Android 15 x86_64 retained the draft, Done item and swipe preference. Android rejected the wrong signer. Offline launch and background/resume passed. [Screenshots and recordings](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/blob/9ed96f934e6dac85a551bb3a0b9e7e44ff8b14e4/docs/validation/android-install/install-update.md).
- Core tests, contract check, lint and typecheck passed. All 2,045 frontend tests passed with one worker. Native lint, all 19 native tests and the web build passed on reruns. The native manifest test initially found two untracked generated files from Track C, which were set aside for the rerun and restored. All 88 rendered tests and the browser capture suite passed.
- GitHub-hosted PR signing proof will run on this draft.

## Open release gate

Focus-dispatch ANRs still occurred during WebView construction on the shared Android 15 emulator after storage moved off the event loop. ADR 0004's startup gate remains open. [Before and after timing and stack findings](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/blob/9ed96f934e6dac85a551bb3a0b9e7e44ff8b14e4/docs/validation/android-install/cold-start.md).

Owner-key signing, the first GitHub Release, and the Nothing Phone (3a) Pro on Android 17 remain post-merge validation.

content.content:
# Android cold startup

## Baseline, 2026-11-22

Android 15, x86_64, emulator-5554, WebView 124.0.6367.219. Tested the
throwaway-signed release at version 0.1.0 (1002), with the manifest and
launcher changes in `67cb852` and local Kotlin and Rust timing markers.
The desktop profile and the old `androidfixture` application were untouched.

Time each Activity marker from entry to `MainActivity.onCreate` using Android
uptime. The frame callback is a Choreographer callback, so it does not measure
the first frame containing the Inbox. Time Rust profile open and setup from
the Tauri setup callback on the Rust event-loop thread. The two timing
origins are independent. The WebView marker measures the callback reporting
its creation, which follows its construction. Focus is the first
`onWindowFocusChanged(true)` marker and does not establish that Android
delivered the input event before its deadline.

| Launch | Host load (1 min) | Frame callback (ms) | WebView callback (ms) | Focus (ms) | Profile open (ms) | Rust setup (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fresh 1 | 1.83 | 229 | 9904 | 14358 | 9078 | 9154 |
| Fresh 2 | 3.46 | 344 | 5805 | 6129 | 4794 | 4905 |
| Fresh 3 | 4.83 | 226 | 6552 | 7401 | 5505 | 5552 |
| Fresh 4 | 6.04 | 85 | 5468 | 6093 | 4342 | 4372 |
| Fresh 5 | 5.44 | 144 | 5018 | 5431 | 5139 | 5176 |
| Populated 1 | 4.91 | 223 | 5617 | 5642 | 3153 | 3160 |
| Populated 2 | 5.46 | 941 | 7914 | 8471 | 6021 | 6055 |
| Populated 3 | 5.24 | 596 | 5134 | 5746 | 3866 | 3875 |
| Populated 4 | 5.12 | 189 | 5628 | 6102 | 4133 | 4143 |
| Populated 5 | 4.78 | 448 | 4899 | 5274 | 3382 | 3385 |

Android reported ANRs for **fresh 1** on PID 31309 and **populated 2** on
PID 866. Both reports arrived after the original sample capture. Android
reported input dispatch waiting 5029 ms and 5003 ms, respectively, for focus.
At the populated report, guest CPU pressure was
`some avg10=88.04`. Android attempted a thread dump, and logcat reported
a timeout and failure to collect the Java and native stacks. This leaves
the direct ANR cause unconfirmed. Focus was recorded before setup
completed for populated 1, showing the Activity main and Rust event-loop
threads can progress independently. Profile open accounted for nearly all
measured Rust startup work, so that is the work to move off the startup
event loop first. WebView initialization and scheduler pressure remain
separate suspects if timeouts recur.

### Reproduction

Before each batch run `pgrep -fa 'cargo|gradle|vitest'` and confirm no active
build. Idle Gradle and Kotlin daemons were present. Record `uptime` per
launch. With the programme lock and T3 device session held, uninstall and
reinstall only the new synthetic test package for each fresh launch. Use
the same APK for all five fresh and five subsequent populated starts.
Launch through the command returned by `device_open` with
`open dev.exedev.emailos --relaunch --no-test-ime`. Take an accessibility
snapshot. Capture timestamped logcat for `EmailOsStartup`,
`RustStdoutStderr`, `ActivityTaskManager` and `ActivityManager`, and match
ANRs to the app PID even if the result arrives after another launch.
The Inbox was confirmed on fresh 1 and after the populated batch.

## After moving Android storage startup off the event loop, 2026-11-22

Same emulator, WebView version and sample method. The diagnostic build used
the production startup changes from `4bb80f5` and `b91f70c`, with local timing
markers and a throwaway signature. No heavy build was active during the
timing runs. The worker columns measure time from entry to the worker.

| Launch | Host load (1 min) | Frame callback (ms) | WebView callback (ms) | Focus (ms) | Rust setup (ms) | Data-path lookup (ms) | Worker total (ms) | ANR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Fresh 1 | 0.32 | 274 | 9407 | 10420 | 0 | 41 | 430 | Yes |
| Fresh 2 | 2.22 | 270 | 8378 | 9364 | 0 | 2 | 347 | Yes |
| Fresh 3 | 2.70 | 212 | 6176 | 6515 | 1 | 1 | 151 | No |
| Fresh 4 | 3.53 | 186 | 7315 | 7655 | 0 | 1 | 85 | No |
| Fresh 5 | 2.73 | 200 | 6629 | 7087 | 9 | 0 | 143 | No |
| Populated 1 | 3.17 | 134 | 6540 | 6950 | 6 | 0 | 65 | No |
| Populated 2 | 3.90 | 70 | 7630 | 8501 | 1 | 1 | 176 | Yes |
| Populated 3 | 4.09 | 186 | 7080 | 7470 | 20 | 2 | 320 | Yes |
| Populated 4 | 4.78 | 417 | 6425 | 6957 | 0 | 2 | 144 | No |
| Populated 5 | 5.19 | 342 | 5767 | 6277 | 0 | 4 | 204 | No |

An intermediate run with only database opening deferred still spent
2.44–6.88 seconds in synchronous Tauri setup across ten samples.
The data path API makes a synchronous Android plugin request, so the final
change resolves it on the worker too. Final Rust setup took 0–20 ms and
the Inbox was confirmed on eight of ten launches. Fresh 1 exposed
the Inbox loading surface at snapshot time. Fresh 2 exposed the Android
**Wait** / **Close app** dialog.

Android DropBox main-thread stacks for fresh 1 (PID 29209) and fresh 2
(PID 29625) both show Android WebView construction, with the former in
`AwContents` calling the input-device Binder service and the latter in
`AwSettings` reading system settings. Guest CPU pressure
`some avg10` was 73.20 and 81.55, respectively. Both app profiles began opening
after the WebView callbacks and focus markers. The captured stacks place
these ANRs in the Android WebView startup path. The samples do not isolate
whether the provider, emulator scheduling or both account for the delay.
The storage fix removed a synchronous dependency. It did not clear the
ANR acceptance gate.

The current app uses AndroidX WebKit 1.6.1 and the emulator has WebView
124. Android's documented asynchronous startup API needs a newer WebKit
library and must complete before the app constructs a WebView to avoid
blocking on pending initialization. These stacks are inside per-instance
construction and do not establish that preinitializing the provider would

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+version=$(node -p "require('./src-tauri/tauri.conf.json').version")
+[[ "$version" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]
+tag="android-v${version}-${ANDROID_VERSION_CODE}"
+mapfile -t apks < <(find src-tauri/gen/android/app/build/outputs/apk -name '*universal*release*.apk')
+[[ ${#apks[@]} -eq 1 ]]
+apk=src-tauri/gen/android/app/build/email-os-android-release.apk
+cp "${apks[0]}" "$apk"
+scripts/android/verify-release.sh "$apk" "$version" "$ANDROID_VERSION_CODE" "$ANDROID_RELEASE_CERT_SHA256"
+# Inspect all releases, including drafts, before changing any remote state.
+gh api --paginate "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=100" --slurp > src-tauri/gen/android/app/build/releases.json
+set +e
+python3 - "$tag" "$ANDROID_VERSION_CODE" src-tauri/gen/android/app/build/releases.json <<'PY'
+import json, re, sys
+pages = json.load(open(sys.argv[3]))
+for release in (r for page in pages for r in page):
+    match = re.fullmatch(r'android-v.+-(\d+)', release['tag_name'])
+    if not match: continue
+    code = int(match[1])
+    if not release['draft'] and code >= int(sys.argv[2]):
+        print('Published release already has this or a higher code'); sys.exit(3)
+    if code == int(sys.argv[2]) and release['tag_name'] != sys.argv[1]:
+        raise SystemExit('Version code belongs to another release')
+PY
+status=$?
+set -e
+if [[ $status == 3 ]]; then exit 0; fi
+[[ $status == 0 ]] || exit "$status"
+previous=$(python3 - src-tauri/gen/android/app/build/releases.json <<'PY'
+import json, re, sys
+releases = [r for page in json.load(open(sys.argv[1])) for r in page if not r['draft'] and re.fullmatch(r'android-v.+-\d+', r['tag_name'])]
+print(max(releases, key=lambda r: int(r['tag_name'].rsplit('-', 1)[1]))['tag_name'] if releases else '140d4e0103c0178afee10ca864fdd7ec344960bf')
+PY
+)
+git merge-base --is-ancestor "$previous" "$GITHUB_SHA"
+# Existing tags must resolve to the exact checked-out commit.
+if git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null; then
+  [[ $(git rev-list -n 1 "$tag") == "$GITHUB_SHA" ]]
+else
+  gh api --method POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" \
+    -f "ref=refs/tags/$tag" -f "sha=$GITHUB_SHA" >/dev/null
+fi
+notes=src-tauri/gen/android/app/build/release-notes.md
+{
+  printf 'Commit: %s\nVersion: %s (%s)\nSize: %s bytes\nSHA-256: %s\n\n' "$GITHUB_SHA" "$version" "$ANDROID_VERSION_CODE" "$(stat -c %s "$apk")" "$(sha256sum "$apk" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
+  "$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/35.0.0/apksigner" verify --print-certs "$apk"
+  printf '\n## Changes\n\n'
+  git log --format='- %s (%h)' "$previous..$GITHUB_SHA"
+} > "$notes"
+if gh release view "$tag" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null | grep -qx true; then

+  gh release upload "$tag" "$apk" --clobber
+  gh release edit "$tag" --notes-file "$notes"
+else
+  gh release create "$tag" "$apk" --draft --title "$tag" --notes-file "$notes" --verify-tag
+fi
+gh release edit "$tag" --draft=false

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+apk=${1:?APK path required}
+expected_version=${2:?version name required}
+expected_code=${3:?version code required}
+expected_cert=${4:?SHA-256 certificate digest required}
+build_tools="${ANDROID_HOME:?}/build-tools/35.0.0"
+badging=$("$build_tools/aapt" dump badging "$apk")

+abis=$(sed -n "s/^native-code: //p" <<< "$badging")
+[[ "$abis" == "'arm64-v8a' 'x86_64'" || "$abis" == "'x86_64' 'arm64-v8a'" ]]
+certs=$("$build_tools/apksigner" verify --verbose --print-certs "$apk")
+actual=$(sed -n 's/^Signer #1 certificate SHA-256 digest: //p' <<< "$certs" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')
+expected=$(tr -d ':' <<< "$expected_cert" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')
+[[ "$actual" == "$expected" && $(grep -c '^Signer #[0-9]* certificate SHA-256 digest:' <<< "$certs") == 1 ]]
+"$build_tools/zipalign" -c -P 16 4 "$apk"

+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import zipfile
+
+with zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]) as apk:
+    libs = [n for n in apk.namelist() if n.startswith('lib/') and n.endswith('.so')]
+    if not libs:
+        raise SystemExit('No native libraries')
+    for name in libs:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryFile(dir=Path(sys.argv[1]).parent) as f:
+            f.write(apk.read(name))
+            f.flush()
+            path = f'/proc/{os.getpid()}/fd/{f.fileno()}'
+            result = subprocess.check_output([sys.argv[2], '-lW', path], text=True)
+        load_segments = [line.split() for line in result.splitlines() if line.lstrip().startswith('LOAD ')]
+        if not load_segments or any(int(segment[-1], 16) < 16384 for segment in load_segments):
+            raise SystemExit(f'{name}: missing or unaligned LOAD segments')
+print('APK metadata, signer, ABIs and alignment verified')
+PY

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+apk=${1:?APK path required}
+expected_version=${2:?version name required}
+expected_code=${3:?version code required}
+expected_cert=${4:?SHA-256 certificate digest required}
+build_tools="${ANDROID_HOME:?}/build-tools/35.0.0"
+badging=$("$build_tools/aapt" dump badging "$apk")
+grep -F "package: name='dev.exedev.emailos' versionCode='$expected_code' versionName='$expected_version'" <<< "$badging"
+abis=$(sed -n "s/^native-code: //p" <<< "$badging")
+[[ "$abis" == "'arm64-v8a' 'x86_64'" || "$abis" == "'x86_64' 'arm64-v8a'" ]]
+certs=$("$build_tools/apksigner" verify --verbose --print-certs "$apk")
+actual=$(sed -n 's/^Signer #1 certificate SHA-256 digest: //p' <<< "$certs" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')
+expected=$(tr -d ':' <<< "$expected_cert" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')
+[[ "$actual" == "$expected" && $(grep -c '^Signer #[0-9]* certificate SHA-256 digest:' <<< "$certs") == 1 ]]
+"$build_tools/zipalign" -c -P 16 4 "$apk"

+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import zipfile
+
+with zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]) as apk:
+    libs = [n for n in apk.namelist() if n.startswith('lib/') and n.endswith('.so')]
+    if not libs:
+        raise SystemExit('No native libraries')
+    for name in libs:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryFile(dir=Path(sys.argv[1]).parent) as f:
+            f.write(apk.read(name))
+            f.flush()
+            path = f'/proc/{os.getpid()}/fd/{f.fileno()}'
+            result = subprocess.check_output([sys.argv[2], '-lW', path], text=True)
+        load_segments = [line.split() for line in result.splitlines() if line.lstrip().startswith('LOAD ')]
+        if not load_segments or any(int(segment[-1], 16) < 16384 for segment in load_segments):
+            raise SystemExit(f'{name}: missing or unaligned LOAD segments')

# Android cold startup

## Baseline, 2026-11-22

Android 15, x86_64, emulator-5554, WebView 124.0.6367.219. Tested the
throwaway-signed release at version 0.1.0 (1002), with the manifest and
launcher changes in `67cb852` and local Kotlin and Rust timing markers.
The desktop profile and the old `androidfixture` application were untouched.

Time each Activity marker from entry to `MainActivity.onCreate` using Android
uptime. The frame callback is a Choreographer callback, so it does not measure
the first frame containing the Inbox. Time Rust profile open and setup from
the Tauri setup callback on the Rust event-loop thread. The two timing
origins are independent. The WebView marker measures the callback reporting
its creation, which follows its construction. Focus is the first
`onWindowFocusChanged(true)` marker and does not establish that Android
delivered the input event before its deadline.

| Launch | Host load (1 min) | Frame callback (ms) | WebView callback (ms) | Focus (ms) | Profile open (ms) | Rust setup (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fresh 1 | 1.83 | 229 | 9904 | 14358 | 9078 | 9154 |
| Fresh 2 | 3.46 | 344 | 5805 | 6129 | 4794 | 4905 |
| Fresh 3 | 4.83 | 226 | 6552 | 7401 | 5505 | 5552 |
| Fresh 4 | 6.04 | 85 | 5468 | 6093 | 4342 | 4372 |

Android reported ANRs for **fresh 1** on PID 31309 and **populated 2** on
PID 866. Both reports arrived after the original sample capture. Android
reported input dispatch waiting 5029 ms and 5003 ms, respectively, for focus.
At the populated report, guest CPU pressure was
`some avg10=88.04`. Android attempted a thread dump, and logcat reported
a timeout and failure to collect the Java and native stacks. This leaves
the direct ANR cause unconfirmed. Focus was recorded before setup
completed for populated 1, showing the Activity main and Rust event-loop
threads can progress independently. Profile open accounted for nearly all
measured Rust startup work, so that is the work to move off the startup
event loop first. WebView initialization and scheduler pressure remain
separate suspects if timeouts recur.

### Reproduction

Before each batch run `pgrep -fa 'cargo|gradle|vitest'` and confirm no active
build. Idle Gradle and Kotlin daemons were present. Record `uptime` per
launch. With the programme lock and T3 device session held, uninstall and
reinstall only the new synthetic test package for each fresh launch. Use
the same APK for all five fresh and five subsequent populated starts.
Launch through the command returned by `device_open` with
`open dev.exedev.emailos --relaunch --no-test-ime`. Take an accessibility
snapshot. Capture timestamped logcat for `EmailOsStartup`,
`RustStdoutStderr`, `ActivityTaskManager` and `ActivityManager`, and match
ANRs to the app PID even if the result arrives after another launch.
The Inbox was confirmed on fresh 1 and after the populated batch.

## After moving Android storage startup off the event loop, 2026-11-22

Same emulator, WebView version and sample method. The diagnostic build used
the production startup changes from `4bb80f5` and `b91f70c`, with local timing
markers and a throwaway signature. No heavy build was active during the
timing runs. The worker columns measure time from entry to the worker.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Fresh 1 | 0.32 | 274 | 9407 | 10420 | 0 | 41 | 430 | Yes |
| Fresh 2 | 2.22 | 270 | 8378 | 9364 | 0 | 2 | 347 | Yes |
| Fresh 3 | 2.70 | 212 | 6176 | 6515 | 1 | 1 | 151 | No |

An intermediate run with only database opening deferred still spent
2.44–6.88 seconds in synchronous Tauri setup across ten samples.
The data path API makes a synchronous Android plugin request, so the final
change resolves it on the worker too. Final Rust setup took 0–20 ms and
the Inbox was confirmed on eight of ten launches. Fresh 1 exposed
the Inbox loading surface at snapshot time. Fresh 2 exposed the Android
**Wait** / **Close app** dialog.

Android DropBox main-thread stacks for fresh 1 (PID 29209) and fresh 2
(PID 29625) both show Android WebView construction, with the former in
`AwContents` calling the input-device Binder service and the latter in
`AwSettings` reading system settings. Guest CPU pressure
`some avg10` was 73.20 and 81.55, respectively. Both app profiles began opening
after the WebView callbacks and focus markers. The captured stacks place
these ANRs in the Android WebView startup path. The samples do not isolate
whether the provider, emulator scheduling or both account for the delay.
The storage fix removed a synchronous dependency. It did not clear the
ANR acceptance gate.

The current app uses AndroidX WebKit 1.6.1 and the emulator has WebView
124. Android's documented asynchronous startup API needs a newer WebKit
library and must complete before the app constructs a WebView to avoid
blocking on pending initialization. These stacks are inside per-instance
construction and do not establish that preinitializing the provider would
remove the stall. Test on a comparable emulator with a newer WebView and
on the physical phone before selecting a provider or lifecycle change.
